# Suññakathā (Ps 2.10)

**ID:** Ps 2.10  
**Section:** Paṭisambhidāmagga (ps)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Suññakathā  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0517m.mul1.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0517m.mul1.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Suññakathā* ("Discussion of Emptiness") is the tenth treatise of the second division (and twentieth treatise overall) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* [Ronkin 2005]. The treatise investigates the qualifier "empty" (*suñña*) and opens by quoting a canonical discourse in which the Venerable Ānanda asks the Buddha why the world is called empty (*suñño loko*), with the Buddha replying that phenomena are empty of a self (*atta*) or anything belonging to a self (*attaniya*) [Ronkin 2005]. The text enumerates and defines twenty-five distinct modes of emptiness, including *suñña-suñña* ("empty of emptiness"), which delineates selflessness in connection with the six sense bases [Ñāṇananda 1971]. Across the treatise, the designation of emptiness is systematically applied to 199 individual phenomena [Stanley]. The *Suññakathā* is also philosophically notable for introducing the term *sabhāva* ("individual essence" or "intrinsic nature") into canonical analysis—qualifying born materiality, feeling, and being as "void of individual essence"—which Bhikkhu Ñāṇamoli highlighted as an exceptionally rare Piṭaka occurrence of the concept outside the *Buddhavaṁsa* [Ronkin 2005; Stanley].

Curated parallels and intertextual citations link the *Suññakathā* directly to the *Suññatalokasutta* (SN 35.85), the *Attadaṇḍasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 15), the *Mogharājamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 19), the *Puggalakathā* of the *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 1.1), and Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* discourse SA 232.

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Mentioned in: SN 35.85 Suññatalokasutta; Mnd 15 Attadaṇḍasuttaniddesa; Cnd 19 Mogharājamāṇavapucchāniddesa; Kv 1.1 Puggalakathā; SA 232 三彌離提

**Sources**

- [Ronkin 2005] Noa Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics: The Making of a Philosophical Tradition (2005) — Structural position as Treatise XX, opening quote from the Saṁyutta on 'suñño loko ti', and the canonical introduction of the concept of sabhāva.
- [Ñāṇananda 1971] Katukurunde Ñāṇananda, Concept and Reality in Early Buddhist Thought (1971) — Enumeration of twenty-five modes of voidness and the explanation of suñña-suñña applied to the six sense bases.
- [Stanley] D. Phillip Stanley, Canons of Tibetan Buddhism in the Context of a Pan-Asian Paradigm (Ph.D. dissertation) — Details regarding the application of void to 199 items and Ñāṇamoli and Warder's remarks on the occurrence of sabhāva.
